DataFinder provides you with a user path analysis tool, which is mainly used to record and analyze the flow process of target users between various pages, and efficiently view and analyze the distribution of user behavior in various pages through visual user traffic flow diagrams. This article provides guidance on using DataFinder's user path analysis tool.

<span id="_1-概念介绍"></span>
# Background information

<span id="_1-1-用户路径"></span>
## Related concepts


|Term |Concept introduction |
|---|---|
|**User Path** & **Path Steps** |**The user path** is the user behavior path, which refers to the statistical distribution of the behavior sequence of a group of users in the product; the user path step refers to the number of path steps that need to be analyzed.<br><br>As shown in the figure below, it is a graph of the user path analysis results after an application is launched. From the start of the application (inclusive), a total of 10 steps of the user's path are analyzed.<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/d52e21c1e78e484cac971b89fabd770e~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |
|**Participate in analyzing events** |"Participatory Analytics Events" refers to user behavior selected to be tracked and analyzed. By analyzing the sequence and flow of these events, it is possible to gain insight into user behavior patterns, preferences, and the efficiency of conversions between different pages or features.<br><br>The events involved in the analysis can be simply divided into:<br><br><br>* **Starting Event ** : The beginning of the user's path, such as the user opening the application (app_launch), visiting the homepage of the website, starting the registration process, etc.<br><br>* **Intermediate events that participate in the analysis ** : various interactions between the user's start event and the end event, such as clicking on the product, browsing the product details, adding to the shopping cart, searching for keywords, watching videos, etc.<br><br>* **Termination event ** : The end of the user's path, which may be the completion of a purchase, successful registration, leaving the app or website, etc., marking the end of a complete process. |


<span id="7b917ede"></span>
## Usage restrictions


* 

* Except for the start event and the end event, there are currently up to 13 intermediate events participating in the analysis that support the analysis.

* Currently, up to 10 user paths are supported for analysis; each step path in the path analysis graph supports up to 10 participating analysis events (maximum number of nodes in a single level).


<span id="_2-快速入门"></span>
# Operation steps

After logging in and entering the DataFinder console, click Analytics \> Advanced Analytics \> User Paths in the top navigation bar to enter the User Paths page and start configuring user path analysis.

<span id="_3-1-选择事件"></span>
## Step1 configuration path

Select the schema for user path analysis to display and configure the events to be analyzed.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/34f2106d7ddc40a6b3576f1a1a6992b2~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


1. Select the mode displayed by the user path analysis, and currently support "migration mode" and "branch mode".

2. Select a start event or a stop event.

   * Switch the upper left corner to "**Start at**" and select the corresponding event, this event is the `starting event`of the user path analysis, that is, this event is the starting point of the user path, and the subsequent behavior path of the starting event is analyzed later.

   * Switch the upper left corner to "**end at**" and select the corresponding event, this event is the `termination event`of the user path analysis, in some cases, we will need to start with certain behaviors to analyze the behavior path (such as analyzing what happened before the user "registration failed"). In these scenarios, it is recommended to configure the `termination event`.

3. Add intermediate events that participate in the analysis.

   Click the **Add Step** button to continuously add multiple intermediate events that need to be analyzed. Currently, up to 13 additions are supported.

4. (Optional) Add a filter for the event.

   Click the Add Filter button after the added event to add a filter for the corresponding event.

5. Configure the analysis scope, support check whether to **also calculate unselected events**.

   Sometimes the user's actual behavior path contains a lot of events that are not configured above, and such users cannot be counted as true churn. The real churn is when users have no follow\-up behavior. Therefore, the DataFinder provides the option to `also calculate unselected events`. When checked, the proportion of users who did not fall into the churn category and hit unselected events can be seen in subsequent user path analysis.

6. Configure the session interval (optional, default is 10 minutes).

7. Configure whether you need to **merge duplicate paths**.

   After checking, the subsequent analysis of data will merge the continuously repeated events in a session into one event to avoid the user path being too long, which is not conducive to business analysis.

   For example, if the business is a social software, the user path will have many repeated operations, such as opening the A conversation box, clicking Send, and then opening the B conversation box. After many operations, the user path will be very long, which is not conducive to analysis. In such scenarios, it is recommended to check.


<span id="_3-2-过滤用户"></span>
## Step2 configuration segmentation filter

You can circle and analyze the target population by attribute filtering, behavioral circling, dynamic circling, and other methods in the segmentation filter, such as screening "users classified as core users, operating systems for iOS and Android, and users with software version 2.0 or above". Configuration operations are consistent with the general capabilities of DataFinder, see details [In-Text Grouping (Segmentation Filtering)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/In-Text_Grouping_Segmentation_Filtering).

<span id="_3-3-属性分组"></span>
## Step3 configuration property grouping

Events are grouped according to an event attribute, and each attribute value is evaluated as an event participating in the analysis.


* For example, the `starting event`selects the product exposure, and the grouping selects the user path according to the product sub\-category, which can be viewed for each product sub\-category.

* When there are too many attribute grouping values, you can filter out attributes that do not need to be viewed by adding filter criteria.


<span id="332af723"></span>
## Step4 View the chart of analysis results

In the chart area below, you can select the data time period to be analyzed, and increase or decrease the number of steps in the user path as needed, as shown in the figure below.

<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c1cea2b1c398402190b9a75ba3772ab4~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>


1. Select the time period to be analyzed in the upper left corner.

   By default, the system automatically displays the last 7 days of user path data,

2. You can add a user path step by clicking the Add Step button in the chart area, or click the added step to delete it.

3. You can set the number of engagement analytics events that appear in each user path step in the chart by clicking the single\-level Maximum Nodes and Advanced Settings buttons in the upper right corner.

   * You can adjust the maximum number of events participating in the analysis at each step by setting the **maximum number of nodes at a single level**, that is, in the user path.

   * You can flexibly adjust to only seeing events where the number of people exceeds a certain value by setting the traffic percentage in the **advanced settings**.

4. View the chart of analysis results. The graph shows all the steps of the user path, as well as the proportion of event traffic and traffic flow under the steps.

   
   |Function point |Function Description |
   |---|---|
   |Result data merge |In addition to the displayed participation analysis events, other events will be automatically merged based on event conversion results, chart display configuration, etc.:<br><br><br>* `Churn`: Users who do not complete the conversion during the window period will be merged into " **Churn**".<br><br>* `More Groupings`: Events exceeding the **maximum number of nodes in a single level** are merged into " **More Groupings**".<br><br>* `Unselected events`: In the above steps, if the **calculation of unselected events at the same time** is checked, the conversion is completed within the window period, but the next step node is composed of unselected events and is merged into " **Unselected events**". |
   |Data details and reanalysis |You can click on the corresponding event in the user path step in the chart to view the data details of this event in the current step, or perform secondary analysis operations such as saving as user grouping and exporting user IDs.<br><br><span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/919fd1462c084999a6a93c7a4c6884de~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |
   


<span id="_3-4-保存到看板"></span>
## Other related operations


* Export analysis images.

   You can click Export in the upper right corner of the chart area to export the analysis result chart as a picture.

* Save the analysis results to the Dashboard.

   You can click `Save to Dashboard`in the upper right corner to add analytical charts that require long\-term monitoring to the Dashboard.


<span id="4aa244cb"></span>
# Calculation logic description

DataFinder will log each user in the selected time range according to the reporting time is sorted, to set the starting event as an example, DataFinder to find the starting event,  **++as long as the time interval between the event analysis does not exceed the set session interval, it is considered in a session ++** .

For example, a user's access behavior is as follows.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">When the same event is visited multiple times, for example, event A is visited multiple times, use "AX" to represent the number of visits X.</div>


If the starting event is set to A, the session interval is 10 minutes, and [A, B, C, D] are the selected 4 path events, then the above is cut into two sessions, which are:


* Session1：

   <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />

* Session2：

   <img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," />


Attention:


* Because E and F are not selected events, the duration of A2 and D is 3 + 3 + 8 = 14 minutes, which exceeds 10 minutes, so the session ends after A2;

* In the example above, A1 \> B \> C \> A2, there are two A events in a session, and A2 is no longer the starting event.


Since the current division time is divided into sessions according to the server level receiving log time, the SDK reports logs in batches of 30s or 1min, so if the time interval is selected at the second level, there will be errors. It is recommended to increase the time interval at the minute level for query analysis.
